correctness.rationale: For coefficients a,b,c of the three pairwise products, the annihilator equations are exactly VH=0 with H the corresponding hollow symmetric matrix. Any nonzero entry h gives a 2-by-2 minor -h^2, so rank(H)>=2 and criticality forces rank(V)<=1. At rank one, V=u(alpha,beta,gamma), and the coefficient-matrix determinant is -2 alpha beta gamma. Thus the origin and exactly the rank-one frames with a zero column are critical. Each support component is an irreducible M-by-2 rank-one cone of dimension M+1. Its image is on the corresponding axis and (e_1,tau e_1,0), and permutations thereof, hit every asserted value. Outside the axes the full Jacobian has rank 3, giving smooth fibers there. On the tau!=0 axis any critical frame must have v_3=0 and v_2 proportional to v_1 with q(v_1)!=0. Over the open q!=0, projecting along v_1 eliminates the two scalar components exactly and leaves the equation B(w_2,w_3)=0 on the two copies of v_1^perp. The Gram matrix is invertible locally over that base; absorbing it into one fiber coordinate system gives the exact split quadratic equation, even Zariski-locally. Its fiber derivatives generate all normal coordinates, and the equation and all base derivatives are in the same ideal. This identifies the full singular scheme with the reduced zero section, of dimension M, and gives the stated completed local ring, rank and multiplicity at every such point. Column permutations handle the other two axes.
residual_risks: The finite-field check is only a control. Its line 46 comment is false for nonzero isotropic spanning vectors, but that comment is not used by the rank test or proof. No claim about a scheme-theoretic discriminant or the full zero-fiber singular scheme was audited as part of this result.
